extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Art of Problem Solving / MathLinks forums (students and community members posting or answering math problems)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for posting mathematical problems, solutions, and other math-related content on the AoPS/MathLinks community forums, including where and how to post, formatting, and etiquette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post each new problem in a new topic
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to post a new problem, post it in a new topic. If you have several problems to post, post every problem in a new topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussing different problems in one topic leads to confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-check problems for mistakes/typos
rubrics_metrics.description: Please double check your problem for mistakes. A simple typo in a formula can make a problem incomprehensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find a typo after posting, edit your message to correct it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give topics useful, descriptive titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Please also give your topic a useful name. Names should describe something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good examples: 'prove concurrency in a right-angled triangle', 'a^4+b^4+c^4\geq a^3b+b^3c+c^3a'. Bad examples: 'hard geometry', 'please help me!!', 'what to do with this one?', 'don't know how to solve it'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the correct forum according to problem level
rubrics_metrics.description: You have to choose the right forum according to its level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forum levels described: High School Basics (standard U.S. high school curriculum; SAT/easy AMC level), Intermediate Topics (harder than basic, e.g. harder AMC/easier AIME), Pre-Olympiad (slightly under olympiad level; many require proofs), Olympiad Section (IMO/USAMO/IMO shortlist level), College Playground (requires college-level knowledge like linear algebra, calculus, topology).

rubrics_metrics.name: High School Basics - appropriate content and difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: High School Basics is for problems that would be considered part of the standard U.S. high school curriculum (generally algebra and geometry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems should be at the SAT or easy AMC 10/12 level and usually should not require complicated proofs; very easy combinatorics or number theory is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate Topics - appropriate content and difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediate Topics is for problems that are harder than 'basic', but not yet approaching the olympiad level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include harder AMC 10/12 problems or easier AIME problems; generally these do not require complicated proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Olympiad - appropriate content and difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-Olympiad is for problems slightly under the olympiad level and for very easy olympiad problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many problems at this level will require proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Olympiad Section - olympiad-level problems and subdivisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Olympiad-level means the level of the IMO, IMO shortlists, the USAMO or the Baltic Way mathematical competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Olympiad Section is subdivided into Algebra, Combinatorics, Geometry, Inequalities, Number Theory and each is further subdivided into Unsolved Problems, Proposed & Own Problems, Open Questions, Solved Problems (archive), and Theorems and Formulas — post to the appropriate subsubforum (e.g., 'Proposed & Own' if you know the solution).

rubrics_metrics.name: College Playground - college-level topics
rubrics_metrics.description: College Playground is a special forum for problems that require knowledge that is usually not given in schools - for instance, linear algebra, calculus, topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this forum for problems needing college-level background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subforum: Unsolved Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Post your problem here if you don't know its solution and you are searching for it, but you know there is a solution (e.g. because the problem was given at an olympiad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for problems known to have solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subforum: Proposed & Own Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Post your problem here if you know the solution and you want to share the problem with others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you have and wish to present your own solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subforum: Open Questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Post your problem here if it is a conjecture, i.e. you don't have its solution and you don't even know whether it has ever been solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for genuine open problems/conjectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subforum: Solved Problems (archive)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the archive for former 'Unsolved' problems which were then solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't post new problems here; it's an archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subforum: Theorems and Formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: This is for important and useful theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for posting notable theorems and formulas rather than problem threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be correct and readable
rubrics_metrics.description: All posts should be correct: strive for no typos and errors, and double-check your message before you post it. Be readable: use LaTeX on your mathematical statements. Write in complete sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX makes it possible to include formulas; learn via the tutorial and test in the Test Forum. Examples in the page show how to write formulas and rendered output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be interesting and/or helpful; avoid empty replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Every post should have some content. A reply that just contains 'it's easy' or 'I solved it' interests no one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanatory content rather than terse claims; meaningful hints or explanations are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't quote whole pages; quote only relevant parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't quote whole pages just to make a one-line answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don't need to quote previous response(s) unless you are responding to a specific portion of someone's earlier post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be appropriate and on-topic; practice good netiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Be appropriate and on-topic: be nice, don't shout or insult, and post only things that fit the topic. Always practice good netiquette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-mathematical discussions in mathematical sections can be considered off-topic and removed; use Round Table or Games & Fun Factory for non-math discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting solutions: understandable but need not be fully detailed
rubrics_metrics.description: The solution needs not be 100% detailed, but it must be understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posts consisting only of words like 'The problem is easy' or 'Cauchy-Schwarz solves it' have no value and may be deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post solutions appropriate to the forum level
rubrics_metrics.description: Please post solutions at your level! If you are an Olympiad-level student, do not post solutions in the 'High School Basics' forum — leave those problems for students at that level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, you may comment on other students' solutions or provide hints if they seem stuck (be polite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Running competitions and homework policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't post problems from running homework competitions! You are supposed to solve them on your own, so making others solve them for you is cheating!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have post-school or university homework problems, indicate that your problems are homework. In most cases, you will get no complete solutions, but hints and other help. Use <hide>text</hide> to hide solutions to avoid spoiling answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using LaTeX for mathematical statements
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX makes it possible to include formulas in your posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: by writing $a^2 + a^3b$ you get rendered math. Learning LaTeX is easy via the short tutorial and by testing it in the Test Forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search before posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you post a new problem, you should ask yourself whether this problem has already been discussed on AoPS/MathLinks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Search function (with keywords and wildcards) and the Resources section (lists of problems by competition). You are not supposed to spend half an hour searching, but try at least once, better twice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other useful/relevant content allowed (within math sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not limited to posting and solving problems. You can write whatever you want, assumed that it is useful and relevant to the forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For instance, you can generalize problems, point out mistakes in others' proofs, ask questions about others' solutions, simplify others' solutions, and so on — but keep to mathematical sections for math content.
